W6 after E065. Time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. The tip is E061: 5.0235 s, 0.7534 on seeds 0–2, 225 steps, population mean ~0.7532.

Mechanisms, with supporting experiments:
1. Accuracy rises with optimizer steps at roughly 0.8–1.5 s/pp. Epoch, step and sample cuts all trade near that dial (E020, E031, E041, E045, E048, E061, E064). E064 (213 steps) read -0.2 pp for -0.19 s, so the free early steps are used up.
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail carries accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share, because it also skips BN/GELU backward and optimizer traffic. It is free only once a block has finished learning (E028, E036, E046, E049 free; E037, E054, E055 costly).
4. Per-step update quality dominates. SGD in place of Muon cost -2.9 pp (E062), ReLU -0.54 pp (E056), stride-2 stem -1.1 pp (E051). Structural swaps are mostly negative.
5. Averaging variants, late LS, warm-up, Lookahead interval and BN recalibration are null or negative. wd ×0.5 gave about +0.2 pp. E065 (anneal-only, time-neutral) read 0.7561 on 3 seeds, so a slower group-1 anneal may be mildly positive. That read is within noise.
6. Noise: the 3-seed mean moves ±0.2 pp across rebuilds of the same commit. Time moves ±0.05–0.1 s. The 20-seed rebuild SD is ≲0.06 pp. Winner's curse is 0.05–0.15 pp.

My misses: E062 and E056 saved more time than I modelled (0.28 s and 0.25 s). My per-step overhead and kernel-cost model has about ±0.1 s of error. I also underrated how much update quality matters. E059 time was higher than I expected, which is build variance.

Unsure: Muon lr and momentum tuning, how much of the freeze cost is anneal versus detach, whether the recipe under-fits, and the PCIe offset.

Expectations: tanh-GELU saves little, and SiLU about the same as GELU. Muon lr and momentum changes are coin flips with a small mean gain. Merging the Muon calls saves about 1%. Any further time cut fails the 0.753 gate on 3 seeds, so the tip is near its limit.

forecasts.reason: The tanh/SiLU saving probably projects below 1.5%, since they move the same bytes and erf is likely not the bottleneck. The idea likely closes with no run, or the run is flat.
About 0.09 s is spent for a gain of 0.05–0.15 pp, which is near the break-even and inside the noise.
Time is unchanged. The accuracy effect is a coin flip with a slight positive lean, because lr was tested only once at 3 seeds.
The merged Muon call is identical math and probably saves about 1%, but a gain that small is hard to confirm against the ±0.07 s time noise.
Momentum 0.6 to 0.8 is a coin flip, with a small lean to harm at this large batch. Time is unchanged.
This is a diagnostic with no recipe change. I expect train top-1 around 85–92%, which means under-fitting.

cruxes: Is the recipe under-fitting? The H8.2.1 train accuracy decides whether optimizer-quality boosters or regularizers are worth testing.
What is the real exchange rate of steps for accuracy (the dial) after E064? It sets the break-even for every cut and top-up.
Is Muon lr or momentum mis-tuned for the 225-step regime? That is the main remaining time-neutral booster.
